name: Dutch Craft Furniture
old_description: Call Us Today!  - Store Hours: Monday-Saturday 9am - 5pm
about:
The company's headquarters are in nearby Millersburg. The founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed. The business began as a retail outlet for furniture crafted by Ohio Amish woodworkers.

The retailer carries an extensive inventory of solid-wood furniture—dining sets, bedroom suites, office pieces, and custom built-in cabinetry—sourced from a network of Amish makers. Its 10,000-square-foot showroom displays a rotating selection of finishes and hardwoods, including walnut, maple, and quarter-sawn white oak. Customers can order custom dimensions, add drawers, or request wood samples before purchasing. The company also provides white-glove delivery and in-home setup throughout the lower 48 states, with no freight shipping.

Dutch Craft Furniture serves primarily residential buyers furnishing homes, as well as commercial clients outfitting offices and hospitality spaces. The product range spans dining rooms, bedrooms, home offices, living rooms, children's rooms, and entryways, plus custom projects such as kitchen cabinets, entertainment units, and home bars.

The company emphasizes direct collaboration with Amish craftsmen, allowing it to offer a wide variety of styles, stains, and paint colors while guiding customers through the selection process. Its differentiators include a large showroom for hands-on evaluation, a wood-sample program, and a delivery model that avoids freight carriers entirely.

name: Dutchland Plastics
old_description: Dutchland specializes in high volume manufacturing of large plastic products and parts.
about:
Dutchland Plastics has operated from Oostburg, Wisconsin since 1967, building a rotational molding business that now spans a nearly 200,000-square-foot facility there and a second plant in Canastota, New York.

The firm specializes in high-volume rotational molding of large plastic parts, producing pieces up to 500 pounds and 17 feet long. Its capabilities cover the full product lifecycle: design and engineering, foam filling, mold-in graphics, robotic and CNC trimming, assembly, and warehousing and distribution. Materials processed include polyethylene, flexible PVC, nylon, and EVA.

Dutchland serves recreational, commercial, outdoor, food and beverage, furniture, marine, and industrial markets. Typical products include kayaks, coolers, jungle gyms, and rotomolded furniture for marine and watercraft applications.

The company positions itself as a turnkey partner for oversized custom projects, emphasizing a "QuickConnect" onboarding program designed to transition production without interruption. Its stated focus is on clients who need to make something really big, offering engineering through to finished-goods shipping under one roof.

name: Dynamic Cable & Security LLC
old_description: Security cameras, Audio Systems, Fiber Splicing Services, TV and Audio Custom Installation, and Custom Display systems.
about:
Based in Yankton, South Dakota, Dynamic Cable & Security LLC draws on more than two decades of field experience in low-voltage systems. The company was founded by a technician who spent 20 years working on fiber optic construction, CCTV, security cameras, audio and video systems, and low-voltage wiring across the Kansas City metro area before returning to Yankton to serve the region.

The firm provides full-service low-voltage solutions, including security camera system design, installation, and maintenance for analog and IP networks; fiber optic splicing, testing, termination, and emergency repair for both aerial and underground plant; whole-home and commercial audio/video design and installation, from home theaters to multi-zone distributed systems and custom display walls; and mobile solar-powered CCTV trailers equipped with 8MP PTZ cameras and license-plate recognition, available for sale or rent. The team reports more than 500 completed jobs and offers 24/7 on-call support across a 250-mile radius covering South Dakota, Nebraska, and Iowa.

Customers range from single-family homes and apartment complexes to farms, commercial businesses, colleges, public schools, and government facilities. The company’s fiber optic services also support telecommunications carriers needing outage response and routine terminations.

Dynamic Cable & Security emphasizes a "big city solutions with a small town feel" approach, backing its security camera installations with a minimum five-year warranty and highlighting its ability to handle everything from routine terminations to complex fiber restoration using specialized tools and hands-on expertise.

The shop specializes in custom plastic fabrication, acrylic fabrication, and plastic machining, producing items such as museum cases, furniture components, lighting accessories, frames, and risers. Work begins with plastic sheets, rods, and tubes that are cut, machined, and finished to customer specifications; the team can also translate sketches or photos into CAD drawings before production. Most projects are made-to-order, though a selection of lighting accessories, frames, and risers is kept in stock.

Customers include retailers, wholesalers, designers, artists, and homeowners across sectors such as furniture, framing, lighting, art enhancement, commercial work, medical supplies, museum cases, pet accessories, restaurant accoutrements, wedding and event displays, and food containers.

The company emphasizes that every project is handled by professional fabrication craftsmen, with attention to detail and quality that it says surpasses overseas or chain-store alternatives. All work is guaranteed, and the business highlights personal relationships and direct access to staff as key differentiators.

name: E-Tronix
old_description: The E-tronix team brings nearly 60 years of experience to the Electronics Assembly sector.
about:
E-Tronix operates from St. Louis Park, Minnesota, as a manufacturers' representative firm covering the Upper Midwest. The company was founded by Erik Stromberg, who had worked for several representative firms in the region since 1998 before launching E-Tronix under the Stromberg Company banner. Stromberg, a University of North Dakota graduate, built the business around a client-first approach and deep industry relationships.

Rather than manufacturing products, E-Tronix represents equipment and materials suppliers for electronics assembly, wire and cable processing, and medical device manufacturing. Its line card includes the LPMS Kappa 1100H low-pressure molding system, Elmotec SolderSmart TOP robotic soldering cells, Hakko FX-971 precision hand-soldering stations, KIC thermal profiling tools, and Nathan Trotter solder alloys. A seven-person team — including a solutions engineer with Daktronics experience and a former Navy electrician's mate who specialized in selective soldering at Pillarhouse — provides technical support, equipment evaluation, and process consulting across Minnesota, the Dakotas, Wisconsin, Iowa, Illinois, Kansas, Missouri, Indiana, and Kentucky.

The firm serves electronic assembly houses, wire-harness shops, and medical-device OEMs. Named references include Daktronics, where Dave Philips credited E-Tronix with guiding equipment selection and implementation, and ProActive PCB, where Paul Schwanbeck highlighted the team's ability to escalate issues through its manufacturer network. E-Tronix also hosts technical webinars on topics such as automatic thermal profiling and next-generation PCB complexity, and exhibits at events like the SMTA Wisconsin Expo and the Electrical Wire Processing Technology Expo.

The company states its differentiation lies in "Partnership," "Solutions Expertise," and "Customer Focus" — summarized as listening and responding in a timely fashion.

name: EBRO Foods Inc.
old_description: Our grandfather founded a food processing plant that with the help of his son, Sr. Manuel “Manny” Abreu, would eventually become one of the largest manufacturing facilities on the island.
about:
EBRO Foods Inc. was founded in 1965 by Manny and Zenaida Abreu in Chicago, Illinois, after the family immigrated from Cuba following the Cuban Revolution. The company’s roots trace back to a food processing plant established by the Abreu grandfather in Cuba, which grew into one of the island’s largest manufacturing facilities. Today, the business remains family-owned and operated across three generations.

The company manufactures authentic Cuban, Mexican, and Latin American food products under the El Ebro and Mexival brands. Production takes place in a 112,000-square-foot USDA-inspected facility that opened in June 2005. Capabilities include product formulation, glass packaging for salsas, and full-scale food manufacturing for the retail market.

EBRO serves the retail grocery trade, supplying Hispanic food products to supermarkets and specialty stores throughout the Midwest. The company describes itself as one of the largest minority-owned food manufacturers in the region.

The Abreu family emphasizes its generational expertise and pioneering role in setting benchmarks for original Hispanic food products.

name: ECM USA
old_description: Lab, university, and research & development heat treat solutions for semiconductor wafer processing
about:
ECM USA operates from Pleasant Prairie, Wisconsin, positioned between Milwaukee and Chicago. The company serves as the American subsidiary of the France-based ECM Group, which consolidates thermal, gas, and atmosphere management expertise across multiple brands headquartered near Grenoble and Montpellier. ECM USA established its Synergy Center in Pleasant Prairie in 2018, housing a NANO vacuum furnace for on-site process development and metallurgical testing.

The company designs and manufactures vacuum furnace systems using cold-wall, electric heating technology that eliminates open flames and enables higher temperature treatments with easy integration into machining lines. Its furnace portfolio includes the ECO double-chamber, JUMBO high-volume, FLEX modular, NANO small-batch, VESUVE nitriding/FNC, FULGURA multi-flow, TURQUOISE horizontal, LILLIPUT hearth-lift, CRISTAL bell, and PFTH vertical oil-quench models, with maximum work zones up to 1,500 mm and load capacities to 2,000 kg. Core processes cover low-pressure vacuum carburizing (LPC), carbonitriding, brazing, sintering, vacuum induction melting, vacuum arc remelting, tempering, vacuum purged gas nitriding, ferritic nitrocarburizing, and vapor-phase aluminizing. Through the ECM Greentech division, it supplies semiconductor wafer-processing furnaces for diffusion, oxidation, doping, and rapid thermal processing up to 300 mm wafers, plus silicon ingot casting and crystal growth equipment. ECM Robotics provides automation integration ranging from cleanroom wafer handling to heavy automotive loads exceeding 1,000 kg.

ECM USA serves the automotive, aerospace, marine, agricultural, semiconductor, solar/photovoltaic, and general industrial heat-treat sectors, as well as university and R&D laboratories. Customers in the United States, Canada, and Mexico include EV transmission manufacturers using LPC, semiconductor fabs requiring wafer processing and SiC crystal growth, and solar producers casting PV silicon ingots. The Synergy Center allows prospective buyers to run low-pressure carburizing and high-pressure gas quenching trials with on-site CMM dimensional measurement, 3D microscopy, and hardness testing before committing to a system purchase.

The company emphasizes that its cold-wall vacuum technology prevents inter-granular oxidation during carburizing, minimizes energy consumption and CO2 emissions, and improves metallurgical properties and process repeatability. Field service, installation, training, and aftermarket parts availability are positioned as integral to the offering, supported by the ECM Group's 50-plus years of engineering and design experience.

name: ECS Sheet Metal
old_description: Providing the Industry with Exceptional Quality Sheet Metal Materials & Services
about:
ECS Sheet Metal operates as a family-owned and operated fabrication shop in Fort Smith, Arkansas. The company, also known as Environmental Control Systems, LLC, has served the region since its founding, though a specific year is not publicly disclosed. The owners emphasize a personal approach, treating every customer like family.

The shop specializes in sheet metal fabrication for HVAC and industrial applications. Core processes include spiral pipe production on a Spiral-Helix 3600 machine, coil line processing on an Engel Coil Line, TDC forming via a Lockformer TDC machine, and clinching with a Tog-L-loc 500. Products range from lock-seam and high-pressure round pipe to rectangular ducts, roof curbs (in stainless steel, phosphatized, galvalume, and aluminum), curb adapters, and custom fabrications. The facility runs modern equipment but does not publish facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures.

ECS primarily serves commercial and industrial contractors across Arkansas and eastern Oklahoma. Its customer base includes mechanical contractors and project managers who need ductwork, curbs, and adapters for rooftop units and ventilation systems. The company highlights its regional focus and repeat business from local clients.

The company differentiates itself through customer service, competitive pricing in its service area, and experienced crews. It states that its commitment to prompt, professional work and the use of current fabrication techniques are what keep customers returning.

old_description: Do to national material shortages, some parts may take longer to ship.
about:
EDCOR Electronics Corporation operates from Carlsbad, New Mexico, where it has been based since January 1991. The company traces its roots to the early 1960s in Utah, where it began as Electronic Development Corporation, a public firm that pioneered wireless microphones and held the first U.S. patent in that field. After several ownership changes and relocations — through Costa Mesa, Irvine, and Santa Ana, California — the management team bought out all shareholders in late 1990, financed the move to New Mexico, and reincorporated the business there.

The company designs and manufactures a broad line of transformers and related components. Its catalog includes audio matching transformers (microphone, line level, combiners, splitters), audio distribution transformers, stereo-to-mono couplers, classic tube audio transformers (single-ended, push-pull, interstage), power transformers for tube and solid-state equipment, chokes and inductors (DC power chokes, high-voltage plate/filament), and a range of parts such as coil bobbins (nylon 6/6 glass-filled), steel laminations, end bells, brackets, and mounting hardware. EDCOR also offers custom transformer design and sells amplifier replacement transformers and kit transformers for brands such as Fender, Dynaco, and Decware.

EDCOR serves professional audio installers, musicians, amplifier builders, and hobbyists. Its distribution transformers were used in the refit of the Rose Bowl in the mid-to-late 1980s. Current customers include tube amplifier designers like Pete Millett and Bruce Heran (OddWatt), kit builders (Decware ZEN kits), and repair shops needing replacements for vintage Fender, Dynaco, and other amplifiers. The company also supports the DIY community with technical blogs and design resources.

EDCOR emphasizes domestic manufacturing: "Proudly designed and built in 'MERICA," with a stated effort to source materials and parts from U.S. suppliers. The transformer production process has evolved over four decades, originally driven by the company's own difficulty in obtaining quality audio and power transformers in the early 1980s, which led to the acquisition of Delta Magnetics and its manufacturing facilities.
